prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-13. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 2.29 |
| Retained earnings       | 1,385M |
| Current liabilities     | 6,019M |
| Current assets          | 13,790M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 18,899M |
| Total liabilities       | 27,401M |
| Total assets            | 58,167M |
| EBIT / operating income | 811M |
| Revenue                 | 5,633M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-13, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided data show moderate leverage (total liabilities/assets of ~47%) and solid liquidity (current ratio of 2.29), but very weak profitability and efficiency (EBIT/assets of only ~1.4%, sales/assets of ~9.7%). Retained earnings are also minimal relative to the asset base (~2.4%), producing an Altman Z-score of ~0.75 that lies well inside the distress zone. These metrics are consistent with a lower-end speculative-grade profile but not yet near-term default territory.
DECISION: B+
